files.sut: collectControls and verifyControls in the shipped controls.mjs, with actual collector subprocesses, normalization transactions, strict contracts, inventoried files, canonical result normalization and report re-verification.
files.claim: The complete controls test file checks targeted mutation attribution, every-selected-case sensitivity, surviving oracles, unrelated failure rejection, setup errors, restored source, tampered evidence, recipe and entrypoint restrictions, stale baseline refusal, and stopping after incomplete permission restoration.
files.oracle: Temporary runners compare actual source data to independently fixed expected values. Three-case fixtures require exact stable ID/status maps: only one selected failure remains unknown, non-target failure remains unknown, and both selected failures kill the control. Other cases assert precise outcomes/diagnostics, actual restored bytes, absence of application on rejected plans, immutable raw-report tamper detection and durable partial rollback status.
files.validity: All eleven runner-expanded cases passed in targeted Vitest execution. The every-versus-some semantic gap now has a mixed two-selected-case counterexample. Setup failures lack valid case evidence and must remain unknown. Fixtures intentionally include a vacuous runner only to prove surviving weak-oracle rejection; it is not claimed as an adequate production test.
files.isolation: Each case gets an OS-created unique temporary root removed in afterEach. Target commands execute that root. The single chmod spy delegates ordinary behavior to the original implementation and is restored in finally; its partial-restoration test verifies later controls stop. No network/service mocks or shared persistent target data are used.
files.determinism: Expected values, case IDs and status arrays are fixed. UUID artifact names are observed rather than asserted. Tests use explicit bounded subprocess timeouts and exact filesystem bytes; no randomized inputs or timing-based success oracle. Filesystem permission behavior assumes the tested POSIX environment.
files.normalization: Tracked changes were made through a complete-content normalization plan and apply receipt. Tests reject test/harness and runner entrypoint edits as negative controls and preserve baseline source after supported mutations. The planned source-only every-to-some sensitivity experiment is separate from these edits and remains unexecuted by this worker.
files.maintainability: A shared fixture constructs single-case targets and a dedicated multi-target helper constructs independent expected-value checks. Parameterized cases name distinct attribution outcomes; full ID/status maps expose which case failed. Existing library and actual-runner qualification boundaries remain separate rather than deleting meaningful overlap.
files.scope: Full semantic source review of all eleven cases in test-conformance-controls.test.ts, including eight existing tests and three new parameterized attribution cases; no sampled case is substituted for another file review. Targeted execution also covers four platform lifecycle and two external-cwd CLI platform cases, seventeen total. Whole repository and other platform controls are outside this review.
